subject: Future Tech
title: Access and Equity
description: A quick win: understand Access and Equity.

hook.text: The first CRISPR cure for sickle cell costs over $2 million. Most patients who need it live in sub-Saharan Africa.

buildup.text: Gene therapies require specialized hospitals, trained staff, and cold-chain logistics that poor countries don't have.

discovery.text: Sickle cell disease kills over 300,000 babies a year, mostly in Africa. The cure exists but can't reach them.

twist.text: Simpler delivery methods are being developed. In-vivo editing that works with a single injection could slash costs.

climax.text: Open-source CRISPR tools and nonprofit biotech firms aim to make gene therapies available everywhere, not the wealthy.

punchline.text: A cure only the rich can afford is not a cure for humanity.

quiz.question: Where does sickle cell disease cause the most deaths?
